description: Distributed tracing decomposed. OpenTelemetry standard. Trace, span, span context, baggage. W3C Trace Context. Sampling strategies (head, tail, adaptive). Backends: Jaeger, Tempo, Zipkin. Correlation with logs + metrics.

sub_mechanisms.name: trace_definition
sub_mechanisms.definition: A complete request flow through services. Identified by trace ID. Composed of spans.
sub_mechanisms.why: Unit of observability for distributed request. Single trace = one user action, all services it touched. Foundation of microservice debugging.

sub_mechanisms.name: span_unit_of_work
sub_mechanisms.definition: A single operation within a trace. Has name, start, end, attributes, status, events. Identified by span ID.
sub_mechanisms.why: Building block. Service A handling request creates span; calls service B which creates child span; etc. Hierarchical structure.

sub_mechanisms.name: span_context
sub_mechanisms.definition: Trace ID + span ID + flags + tracestate. Propagated across service boundaries.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without context propagation, child spans can't link to parent. W3C Trace Context standardised the propagation format. Headers: traceparent, tracestate.

sub_mechanisms.name: baggage_propagation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Key-value pairs propagated with trace. Application-specific data flowing with request.
sub_mechanisms.why: Distinct from trace metadata: passes app data (user ID, tenant) across services. Used for routing, filtering, custom telemetry.

sub_mechanisms.name: OpenTelemetry_standard
sub_mechanisms.definition: CNCF standard for telemetry: API + SDK + protocol (OTLP) + auto-instrumentation. Merged OpenTracing + OpenCensus.
sub_mechanisms.why: Universal API independent of backend. Code uses OTel; export to Jaeger, Tempo, Datadog, etc. Eliminates vendor lock-in. Industry consolidation.

sub_mechanisms.name: auto_instrumentation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Agent attaches at runtime; instruments common libraries (HTTP, DB, gRPC) automatically.
sub_mechanisms.why: Java agent, Python opentelemetry-instrument, .NET profiler. No code changes for common instrumentation. Manual for custom spans.

sub_mechanisms.name: head_based_sampling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Sampling decision at trace start. Random N% or rate-limited. Simple, no buffering.
sub_mechanisms.why: Most common. Cost: lose data for important-but-unsampled traces. Variants: parent-based (child follows parent decision).

sub_mechanisms.name: tail_based_sampling
sub_mechanisms.definition: Buffer all spans; sample based on trace properties (errors, slow). Decide after seeing complete trace.
sub_mechanisms.why: Captures all errors + slow traces. Cost: memory for buffer, dedicated tail-sampling collector. Modern observability stack.

sub_mechanisms.name: Jaeger_backend
sub_mechanisms.definition: CNCF tracing backend. Created by Uber. Cassandra/Elasticsearch/Badger storage. Web UI for trace visualization.
sub_mechanisms.why: Open source standard. UI shows trace as Gantt chart. Query by service + operation + tags. Widely deployed.

sub_mechanisms.name: Grafana_Tempo
sub_mechanisms.definition: Object-storage-backed traces. Optimised for cost: only store, no index. Query via trace ID.
sub_mechanisms.why: Massive scale at low cost. Trade: can't search 'all traces with error' — only retrieve by ID. Pair with logs/metrics that have IDs.

sub_mechanisms.name: exemplars_metrics_to_traces
sub_mechanisms.definition: Histogram metrics linked to representative traces. Click latency bucket → see traces in that bucket.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bridges metrics + traces. Saw p99 spike at 14:00 → click to see actual slow traces. Critical for root cause analysis.

sub_mechanisms.name: logs_to_traces_correlation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Logs include trace_id + span_id. Click log entry → view trace.
sub_mechanisms.why: Unifies observability pillars. See error log → jump to trace. See slow trace → jump to logs from that request. Foundation of modern observability UX.

derivation_rules.name: trace_context_essential_for_microservice_observability
then: without trace context, observability is N independent views
derivation_rules.why: Each service's logs/metrics describe its own work. Trace context links them: 'these all came from same request'. Without it: piecing together flow is manual + error-prone.

derivation_rules.name: tail_sampling_captures_outliers_head_sampling_loses_them
if: only 1% of traces are sampled at head
then: 1% of error traces are captured (miss most)
derivation_rules.why: Head sampling random: errors as likely as success to be sampled. Tail sampling sees complete trace, prioritises errors / slow. Modern stacks use tail for outliers, head for baseline.

derivation_rules.name: OpenTelemetry_eliminates_vendor_lock_in
if: telemetry is generated via OTel SDK
then: backend can be swapped without code changes
derivation_rules.why: Universal API + OTLP protocol. Today export to Jaeger; tomorrow Tempo or Datadog; no code change. Industry consolidation after years of fragmentation.

derivation_rules.name: auto_instrumentation_minimal_friction
then: existing services gain tracing without code changes
derivation_rules.why: Java agent attaches at JVM start; instruments HTTP, DB, gRPC. Manual instrumentation needed only for custom spans. Practical adoption path.

derivation_rules.name: exemplars_bridge_metrics_to_traces
derivation_rules.why: See p99 spike at 14:00 → click bucket → see actual slow trace → diagnose. Without exemplars: 'p99 is bad' but no path to specific request. Major UX improvement.
